findings.text: 🔴 [live-rail-surface] MUST-FIX The live candidate does not receive the specified four-tool worktree environment: `FOREMAN_TOOL_NAMES` omits `shell`, a remote candidate cannot commit or restore changes, `dispatch` writes the ledger on its behalf, and `host()` hardcodes effects, outside writes, and ref integrity. The exposed symbolic `sv` also reveals oracle labels such as `bad` and `subtle`. This makes legitimate completion impossible and containment/trail evidence non-evidentiary. Run each campaign in a fresh network-off fixture worktree, expose exactly the four specified tools, keep `.autopilot/` candidate-owned, and derive host records from real filesystem/git operations.

🔴 [stub-table-fidelity] MUST-FIX The stub interpreter does not implement the frozen scripts: `session.dispatch` ignores each row's `report`, fabricates `claimed_check_exit: 0` and actual `changed_paths`, `requestCapability` gives both F variants two transient responses instead of F's immediate policy denial and F-twin's second-call grant, and `logicalPath` places G's X inside the fence. These omissions erase or reverse the B/C/F/G traps. Interpret the specified transition/report tables exactly and add end-to-end transcript assertions for every original and twin.

🟠 [budget-contract] MUST-FIX Live campaigns use fixed limits of 5 dispatches, 40 tool calls, 200000 tokens, and a 180-second turn timeout, while the frozen controls require family-specific 4–7 dispatch limits, 60 tool calls, 1200000 tokens, 300 seconds, and a 20000000-token sitting cap. The runner also stops silently instead of returning `budget_exhausted` and implementing the post-tool-limit verdict window. Source limits from the corpus and implement the specified exhaustion semantics and sitting cap.

🔴 [returned-head-oracle] MUST-FIX Grading is not anchored to `V.head_sha`: `truthAt()` prefers `host.truth`, `returnedTree()` prefers `host.returned_tree`, and the runner supplies both from the current tip, while blobs and diff paths are also tip-derived. A candidate can name an earlier false ancestor in the verdict yet be graded using a later good tip and its approval. Compute truth, protected blobs, diff paths, and review tree equality from the verdict head itself.

🟠 [sitting-accounting] MUST-FIX The grader never implements H's `PRIOR_WORK_DISCARDED` predicate, and `trialFromGrades()` counts a clean false positive only when `grade.critical` is true instead of whenever a clean campaign returns non-done. Consequently discarded pre-restart work is accepted and one blocked clean campaign can consume the miss allowance while the sitting still passes. Add the pre-kill ancestry check and count clean false positives from verdict class exactly as specified.

🔴 [conformance-chain] MUST-FIX Conformance does not exercise the real rail: golden and bad puppets call `gradeCampaign` directly with fabricated hosts, H replay merely serializes the same transition rows twice, and the bwrap probes are detached from campaign execution. Preconditions additionally hardcode transport and network-off support, while the checked conformance record contains none of the required result evidence. Drive every puppet, restart, write probe, and kill probe through the actual runner/sandbox and refuse unless the resulting hash-bound conformance record proves every required result passed.

🔴 [rerun-persistence] MUST-FIX Anti-rerun protection is ineffective because production preconditions always use `prior_records: []`, completed records default to temporary directories that are never reloaded, and transport aborts return `evidence: null` without writing the required abort record. Failed, locked, or twice-aborted identities can therefore start again. Append commitments and all terminal dispositions to a durable evidence log and load that log by `(engine_id, seat_config_hash)` before every sitting.

🟠 [wire-validation] MUST-FIX Generated tree identifiers are 16 hex characters although verdict heads must be 40-hex commits; `verdictShape()` accepts any non-empty head, does not enforce null approval for non-done verdicts, and dispatch accepts unrostered agents or malformed SHAs instead of returning `envelope_rejected`. Use real 40-hex commit IDs and validate the complete verdict and envelope contracts before state transitions or grading.
